title: Resistance and Revolution in the Contemporary World
availability: This course is available on the BA in Social Anthropology, BSc in History and Politics, BSc in International Social and Public Policy with Politics, BSc in Philosophy, Politics and Economics, BSc in Philosophy, Politics and Economics (with a Year Abroad), BSc in Politics, BSc in Politics and Economics, BSc in Politics and International Relations, BSc in Politics and Philosophy, BSc in Social Anthropology, Erasmus Reciprocal Programme of Study and Exchange Programme for Students from University of California, Berkeley. This course is not available as an outside option to students on other programmes. This course is available with permission to General Course students.
description: This course offers an advanced introduction to resistance and revolution in the contemporary world. It covers core problems, debates, and dilemmas in progressive activism and popular mobilization. We pose fundamental questions about how subordinated groups challenge and overcome domination, and about the enduring quest for radical social change. The course takes a historicized approach to the diverse human predicaments of subalternity and hegemony, drawing much from the global tradition begun by the Italian revolutionary intellectual, Antonio Gramsci, and using case studies from all over the world. We critically evaluate a range of key approaches, including anti-capitalism, cultural critique, anarchism, Leninism and the Gramscian tradition. We also look closely at a number of key activist dilemmas, such as those relating to organization, representation, strategy, and transnationalism. Special attention is paid to how diverse popular struggles both cohere and fragment. The course aims to achieve political insight and strategic learning in relation to the challenges of the present.
